newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-COUPLES' MIND ON SICK FATHER.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-COUPLES' MIND ON SICK FATHER.

text.p: Fred Couples was "thrilled" with his two-under-par 69 in the windy opening round of the British Open on Thursday but said his sick father was uppermost in his thoughts.
The American's 74-year-old father Tom has been receiving chemotherapy for leukaemia in recent months and Couples said: "I'll call him as soon as I get back to my room.
"He became sick three months ago and lost 35lbs (16 kg), but he's back home now and putting on weight again.
"I took a month off before the U.S. Open, didn't touch a club and didn't feel like playing. It wears on you."
Couples, the 1992 Masters champion and former world ranked number one player, has a best British Open finish of tied third in 1991 but has had a pretty thin time in the competition since then.
"I would love to win another Major and my best chances are here and at the U.S. Masters," he said. "But it's been a difficult year, I've not played much lately and could shoot anything tomorrow.
"The back nine here is about as hard a nine as you will ever play so I am thrilled with the round.
"I fell in love with the British Open from the first time I came here in 1984 and finished fourth at St Andrews. I love playing here -- the courses are fantastic, as are the galleries."
Couples was introduced to golf by his father, who worked for the Seattle Park and Recreation Department.
"He was a baseball player and used to take me to soccer and baseball. He gave me the gift of being an athlete. His influence was that he loved sports."

Couples blazed the front nine, turning in five-under-par 31. But as he hit the headwind he suffered, bogeying the next two holes and having to sink 20ft and 15ft par-saving putts at the 15th and 17th.
He then bogeyed the last, missing from five feet to slip to two-under.
